name: Use chopsticks extremely well
blurb: Not just managing, but eating anything — a slippery mushroom, a single grain of rice, a peanut — with a relaxed, correct grip.
gear: A pair of wooden or bamboo chopsticks (slipperier than plastic but grippier on food)
steps: Fix the grip: the lower stick rests still in the crook of your thumb and on your ring finger; only the upper stick moves, held like a pencil.
Practise opening and closing the upper stick alone, without the lower one moving at all.
Pick up increasingly awkward objects: cubes, then beans, then a single peanut, then a single grain of rice.
Eat every meal you reasonably can with them for a week, including hard cases like noodles and tofu.
Learn the etiquette: never stand them upright in rice, never pass food chopstick to chopstick, never spear food.
tips: The most common fault is moving both sticks. If the bottom one wanders, your grip is too high or too tense.
Hold them roughly two-thirds of the way up. Gripping near the tips halves your reach and control.
proof: You pick up a single grain of rice, and eat a whole meal without switching to a fork.
